data.domain: Homelessness and housing-transition services in Wichita–Sedgwick County, Kansas. Nearly every record is about a handoff between agencies: youth leaving foster care, families looping through 211, and adults blocked at shelter doors, document offices and rental screening. Confidence HIGH; it rests on the shelter, intake, program, document and rehousing records.
data.hero_title: Wichita houses people fast once they are matched; the losses happen between its doors
data.hero_lead: Wichita reaches housing in [[community-snapshot.avgDaysToHousing]] days, against [[community-snapshot.nationalDaysToHousing]] days nationally. Even so, only [[status001-reachable]] of [[status001-total]] emergency beds are reachable tonight, and youth leave care into a documents-and-benefits maze [CHALLENGE_DATA: community-snapshot, system-status]. Steady Path puts a named navigator and a shared handoff board on top of the assets Wichita already runs.
data.summary_title: Only [[status001-reachable]] emergency beds are reachable tonight; the fix is the handoff, not another front door
data.bluf_text:
Wichita's system is fast once a person is matched, but it loses people at the transfers between agencies. The evidence:
  • [[community-snapshot.avgDaysToHousing]] days to housing against [[community-snapshot.nationalDaysToHousing]] days nationally [CHALLENGE_DATA: community-snapshot].
  • Only [[status001-reachable]] of [[status001-total]] emergency beds are reachable now [CHALLENGE_DATA: system-status].
  • [[transition-programs.prog-006.transitionDropoutRate]] of CrossRoads exits have no confirmed next placement [CHALLENGE_DATA: transition-programs].
Steady Path spends [[budget]] on navigators who carry each person across those transfers. It adds a bottleneck dashboard layered on Second Light coordinated entry, and uses the brief's [[reserve]] reserve to win landlord and youth trust. It targets [[beneficiaries_y1]] people in Year 1 at [[cpb_y1]] per person. Without it, valued outcomes estimated at [[coi_3yr]] would not happen over [[plan.years]] years [ESTIMATE].
data.decision_text:
Approve a [[pilot_days]]-day pilot inside the [[budget]] contract, with renewal tied to the gate in the renewal case.
  • Python's estimate of valued outcomes forgone without the program is [[coi_3yr]] over [[plan.years]] years.
  • That figure excludes housing placements. The data holds no local cost of a shelter night, so housing is reported as a count, not a dollar value.
data.crisis_title: [[community-snapshot.shelteredAndUnshelteredTotal]] people were homeless on the count night, and most failures happen between agencies
data.crisis_body:
On the Point-in-Time night, [[community-snapshot.shelteredAndUnshelteredTotal]] people were homeless, [[community-snapshot.unshelteredHeadcount]] of them unsheltered. That total was [[community-snapshot.yoyChangePct]] higher than in 2024 [CHALLENGE_DATA: community-snapshot]. Speed is not the problem: housing takes [[community-snapshot.avgDaysToHousing]] days against [[community-snapshot.nationalDaysToHousing]] days nationally, and the local rate of [[community-snapshot.perCapitaRateLocal]] sits below the national [[community-snapshot.perCapitaRateNational]]. Reach is the problem.
  • Only [[status001-reachable]] of [[status001-total]] emergency beds are reachable now [CHALLENGE_DATA: system-status].
  • Of [[beds_online_all]] beds online, [[free_beds_all]] sit free, but entry rules screen most people out [CHALLENGE_DATA: shelter-inventory].
  • Youth face the steepest cliff. Homelessness among youth from foster care reaches [[community-snapshot.fosterHomelessnessAge21]] by age 21, above the national [[ext.us_poverty_rate_2023]] poverty rate. These are different measures, so the comparison shows scale only (LOW confidence as like-for-like).
  • The KanCare extension loses [[transition-programs.prog-003.transitionDropoutRate]] of enrollees, above the national [[ext.us_uninsured_rate_2023]] uninsured rate. This is again a different measure (MEDIUM confidence) [CHALLENGE_DATA: transition-programs].
data.crisis_human:
Maya, [[q.4f218]], has a CrossRoads bed this week but no birth certificate, so a Kansas state ID is at least [[state_id_days]] days away [CHALLENGE_DATA: stabilization-docs].
  • Income poverty: entry jobs pay [[q.43a8c]].
  • Transportation poverty: a bus pass costs [[q.c9ad8]] a month on buses with [[q.2bfae]]-minute headways, so every trip to DCF, SSA or City Hall costs her a shift.
  • Language barriers: H.O.T., CrossRoads Youth Intake, Second Light Coordinated Entry and the Family Promise Intake Line list English only [CHALLENGE_DATA: intake-network]. Spanish-speaking households like those Denise navigates beside lose doors entirely.
  • The age cliff makes each barrier worse: DCF IL ends the day she turns [[q.cc62b]], and every move that finds her a bed sends KanCare notices to an old address.
That is how the extension loses [[transition-programs.prog-003.transitionDropoutRate]] of enrollees [CHALLENGE_DATA: transition-programs].
data.crisis_sources: [CHALLENGE_DATA: community-snapshot, system-status, shelter-inventory, intake-network, transition-programs, stabilization-docs]. National benchmarks: Census Bureau P60-283 (poverty) and Health Insurance Coverage in the United States: 2023. The data holds no neighborhood-level income, poverty or coverage rates, so the personas cite system-level figures only.
data.solution_title: A named navigator carries each transition for [[beneficiaries_y1]] people in the first year
data.solution_body:
Steady Path assigns [[model:3|navigators]] navigators who own each handoff from first contact to keys in hand. A shared bottleneck dashboard sits on top of Second Light coordinated entry, where HMIS bed-matching is not yet live [CHALLENGE_DATA: system-status]. The pilot has five working parts:
  • Warm handoffs. Every CrossRoads exit, every 211 Kansas after-hours loop and every H.O.T. contact gets a logged transfer. Today about [[q.08402]] 211 callers loop back [CHALLENGE_DATA: intake-network].
  • Document fast-lane. City ID through Breakthrough Wichita attestation, then birth certificate, Social Security card and state ID in parallel. Open Door shelter-address letters solve the residency step [CHALLENGE_DATA: stabilization-docs].
  • Benefits guard. Navigators file the KanCare address change and flag expedited [[q.f7827]]-day SNAP.
  • Youth pathways. DCF IL, ETV and SOUL Family enrollment for aging-out youth. [[programs.free]] of [[programs.listed]] transition-program slots are free [CHALLENGE_DATA: transition-programs].
  • Housing pathways. Landlords like Luis get a single contact through NEXTenant, feeding rapid rehousing and the HumanKind Housing First pathway [CHALLENGE_DATA: rehousing-options].
data.solution_population:
The program targets [[beneficiaries_y1]] people in Year 1, scaling to [[beneficiaries_y3]] by Year 3. They come from a larger pool:
  • The homeless-services system served [[community-snapshot.peopleServedAnnual]] people in FY 2023–24, of whom [[community-snapshot.firstTimeHomelessAnnual]] were homeless for the first time.
  • [[community-snapshot.shelteredAndUnshelteredTotal]] people were homeless on the Point-in-Time night [CHALLENGE_DATA: community-snapshot].
The data lists facilities, not neighborhoods or ZIP-level areas, so this proposal states no count of monitored areas. Year-1 reach rests on caseload: [[model:3|navigators]] navigators at [[model:80|people per navigator per year]] people each, on episodes the length of the [[pilot_days]]-day pilot [ESTIMATE].
data.cost_of_inaction:
Python computes the yearly cost of inaction from the valued outcomes: KanCare-protected ER visits avoided, expedited SNAP secured, and ETV education funding unlocked. Each year's figure is those outcomes for that year's people served, less deadweight of [[deadweight]].
  • Year 1: [[coi_y1]]
  • Year 2: [[coi_y2]]
  • Year 3: [[coi_y3]]
  • Cumulative over [[plan.years]] years: [[coi_3yr]]
Stable housing placement is material but not valued, because the data gives no local cost of a shelter night or a return to homelessness. The figure therefore understates what is lost. The SROI uses the same outcome list but goes further: it also nets out attribution, displacement and drop-off, and discounts over [[sroi_horizon_years]] years. That is why the SROI's [[sroi_pv_benefits]] is smaller per person than the cost-of-inaction figure [ESTIMATE].

data.evidence_title: [[transition-programs.prog-006.transitionDropoutRate]] of CrossRoads youth exits leave without a confirmed next placement

evidence_cards.title: Beds exist but cannot be reached
evidence_cards.body: Alert status-001 counts [[status001-reachable]] reachable beds of [[status001-total]], or [[calc:pct_of|status001-reachable|status001-total]]. Referral rules, sobriety screening and household restrictions block the rest. Union Rescue Mission's breathalyzer gate alone filters out [[q.1f31c]] of would-be intakes. This pattern mirrors a mechanism documented in national shelter research: conditional entry rules leave beds empty while unsheltered people with active substance use or mixed households are turned away within minutes of arriving at the door.

evidence_cards.title: Youth shelter exits fall into a gap
evidence_cards.stat_label: of CrossRoads exits with no confirmed next placement
evidence_cards.body: CrossRoads is the only round-the-clock low-barrier youth shelter. BRIDGES downstream has [[q.ed5fc]] units, a [[q.536a6]]-week wait and [[q.60225]] realistic admits. DCF IL loses [[q.84d8e]] participants within [[q.4a2ab]] days of exit. This pattern mirrors the age-out cliff described nationally for foster youth: support ends on an administrative date rather than when housing is stable, and housing loss follows within months of that exit.

evidence_cards.title: Health coverage is lost to paperwork, not eligibility
evidence_cards.stat_label: dropout from the KanCare extension for former foster youth
evidence_cards.body: The extension has no income test and [[transition-programs.prog-003.activeEnrollment]] active enrollees. Coverage is lost mainly when recertification notices go to old addresses, and re-enrollment requires an in-person DCF visit with a [[q.501c0]]-hour wait. This pattern mirrors the administrative-churn mechanism documented in national Medicaid research: eligible people lose coverage within weeks of a move because mail no longer reaches them.

evidence_cards.title: Matched people are housed fast
evidence_cards.stat_label: average days to housing in Wichita
evidence_cards.body: The national figure is [[community-snapshot.nationalDaysToHousing]] days, [[calc:times|community-snapshot.nationalDaysToHousing|community-snapshot.avgDaysToHousing]] the local time. Retention after placement is [[community-snapshot.permanentRetention2yr]]. The system's back end works, which points the money at the front-end handoffs. This pattern mirrors the Housing First evidence documented nationally, where people placed without preconditions mostly stay housed within the years after move-in.

data.operations_title: A shared handoff board joins [[intake-network.count]] separate front doors into a tracked path
data.operations_description:
Steady Path runs as a thin coordination layer, not a new front door. It has four moving parts:
  • Intake. People arrive through the existing doors: 211 Kansas, H.O.T., Open Door, CrossRoads Youth Intake, Second Light Coordinated Entry and the DCF Wichita Service Center [CHALLENGE_DATA: intake-network]. Partner staff open a case on the shared board. A navigator triages it the same business day using the published prioritization table: a bed tonight, a transition program, or a door to walk into.
  • Bottleneck dashboard. It shows reachable beds by entry condition and free transition slots ([[programs.free]] of [[programs.listed]]). It also shows wait clocks: HumanKind [[q.db126]] weeks, BRIDGES [[q.536a6]] weeks, Family Promise [[q.970ad]] weeks, and a COMCARE assessment of [[q.83dac]] weeks [CHALLENGE_DATA: shelter-inventory, transition-programs].
  • Parallel tracks. Navigators run three at once:
    • documents: City ID, birth certificate, Social Security card, state ID;
    • benefits: KanCare address update, expedited SNAP, ETV;
    • housing: NEXTenant partners, rapid rehousing through Salvation Army and Hilltop Village, the HumanKind Housing First waitlist, and VASH for veterans like Robert.
  • Follow-through. Every case closes only after a check-in at the end of its episode.
data.plan_title: A [[pilot_days]]-day pilot that ends at a written renewal gate
data.sensitivity_text: Python's stress case reaches [[stress_beneficiaries_y1]] people, [[calc:pct_less|stress_beneficiaries_y1|beneficiaries_y1]] fewer than planned, on the same Year-1 expenses of [[total_exp_y1]]. Cost per person then rises to [[stress_cpb_y1]], against the base case's [[cpb_y1]]. The pilot's main exposure is therefore reach, not spending: if navigators cannot reach enough people, cost per person climbs. That is why the dashboard tracks new cases weekly from launch.
data.renewal_label: Renewal gate at the end of the [[pilot_days]]-day pilot
data.renewal_text:
Renew only if the pilot shows that handoffs, not new capacity, move people. The gate has four tests:
  • [[model:80%|target share of CrossRoads exits with a confirmed next placement]] of CrossRoads exits leave with a confirmed next placement, against [[transition-programs.prog-006.transitionDropoutRate]] leaving without one today.
  • [[model:85%|target share of enrolled former foster youth whose KanCare extension remains active at pilot end]] of enrolled youth keep KanCare coverage active at pilot end.
  • The median time from zero documents to a state ID is at or below [[model:35|days, target median from no documents to state ID]] days, against a processing floor of [[state_id_days]] days.
  • [[model:75%|target share of referrals completed as logged warm handoffs]] of referrals are logged as warm handoffs.
On the base case, Year 3 cost per person is [[cpb_y3]]. The SROI is [[sroi]], and it is partial because housing is not valued.
data.appendix_title: Every figure traces to [[data.record_count]] records fetched at run time
data.methodology:
• Cross-referencing. We matched each shelter's entry conditions against the reachable-bed alert, each youth program's age cap and dropout rate against the document chain, and each rehousing option's screening against voucher acceptance.
  • Where the records agree. The shelter, intake and program records all point to the same place: failures cluster at transfers between agencies (after-hours, at shelter exit and at address changes), not at the housing match itself. Wichita's own days-to-housing and retention figures confirm a strong back end (HIGH confidence).
  • Benchmarks. National benchmarks (Census poverty and uninsured rates, the AHRQ ER visit cost, BLS wages) are used for context and valuation only. Where a benchmark measures something different from the local figure, we say so (LOW to MEDIUM confidence for those comparisons).
  • Caveats. Rates whose denominators the data does not state, such as the share housed within the year, are cited as the data writes them.
data.ai_process:
• Every endpoint of the challenge API was fetched at run time and passed to claude-opus-5-5 (effort high) as raw JSON. That call wrote this narrative, the financial assumptions and the brief answers.
  • Python computes the financial model, cost per person, SROI and cost of inaction from those assumptions. It also writes the workflow diagram's Mermaid code and tooltips from the registry.
  • A further claude-opus-5-5 call (effort medium) writes the KPI framework, failure modes, renewal gate, thesis and judge questions. Python checks every id, fund line, risk and day in that output.
  • Every quantity on the page is a registry token, and a checker counts how many trace to it.
  • The page's chat answers from a context file through a server-side proxy.
assumptions: Year-1 reach: [[model:3|navigators]] navigators at [[model:80|people per navigator per year]] people each, using episodes sized to the [[pilot_days]]-day pilot, gives [[beneficiaries_y1]] people [ESTIMATE].

Outcome rates apply to people served, not to the [[community-snapshot.shelteredAndUnshelteredTotal]] counted on the Point-in-Time night: [[model:30%|share of people served avoiding an ER visit through kept KanCare coverage]] avoid an ER visit, [[model:25%|share of people served securing expedited SNAP]] secure expedited SNAP, and [[model:5%|share of people served unlocking ETV funding]] unlock ETV funding.

Deadweight is [[deadweight]], and attribution to partners is [[model:30%|share of outcomes attributed to partner agencies]]. Many outcomes would partly happen through Open Door and Center of Hope benefits navigators anyway.
Program Director oversight is provided in kind by the coalition (United Way of the Plains). The personnel cap of [[cap.personnel_y1]] funds frontline navigators instead.
Indirect costs use the de minimis rate of [[ext.indirect_deminimis_rate]] of modified total direct costs.
The HMIS bed-matching layer at Second Light is not live during the pilot. The shared board is a lightweight layer that partners update by hand [CHALLENGE_DATA: system-status].
Growth: [[model:20%|growth in people served, Year 2]] in Year 2 and [[model:15%|growth in people served, Year 3]] in Year 3, limited by navigator hiring rather than demand.

sroi_outcomes.category: CrossRoads youth exits with a confirmed next placement
sroi_outcomes.why: This is an intermediate step toward housing. Valuing it as well as the housing outcome would count the same benefit again.
Documents are an input to the benefits, housing and work outcomes already listed. Counting them separately would overstate value by counting the same benefit again.

phases.summary: Stand up: hire, sign data agreements, build the board
phases.content:
• Hire the navigators.
  • Sign case-sharing agreements with Second Light, CrossRoads, Open Door, 211 Kansas, H.O.T. and the DCF Wichita Service Center [CHALLENGE_DATA: intake-network].
  • Configure the bottleneck dashboard: reachable beds by entry condition, free transition slots, wait clocks and the document pipeline.
  • Open landlord conversations through NEXTenant.
  • Train partner intake staff to flag expedited SNAP and KanCare address changes.
  • Start the youth peer-ambassador and landlord outreach lines from the marketing reserve.

phases.summary: Run live handoffs across youth, family and adult paths
phases.content:
• Take every CrossRoads exit, every 211 Kansas after-hours loop and every H.O.T. contact onto the board.
  • Run the document fast-lane with Breakthrough Wichita: City ID, then birth certificate, Social Security card and state ID [CHALLENGE_DATA: stabilization-docs].
  • Enroll eligible youth in DCF IL, ETV and SOUL Family.
  • Route families to rapid rehousing at Salvation Army and Hilltop Village, adults to the HumanKind Housing First waitlist, and veterans to VASH.
  • Review bottlenecks weekly with partners.

phases.summary: Measure, follow up and decide renewal
phases.content:
• Complete follow-up check-ins for every open case.
  • Report against the renewal gate: confirmed placements at CrossRoads exit, KanCare coverage kept, days from zero documents to state ID, and the warm-handoff share.
  • Publish the dashboard to the coalition's [[community-snapshot.coalitionMemberOrgs]] member organizations.
  • Deliver a written renewal recommendation to the City with the base-case cost per person.

risks.risk: Downstream capacity stays saturated. BRIDGES has [[q.ed5fc]] units and HumanKind's waitlist runs [[q.db126]] weeks, so navigators confirm next steps that cannot be filled.
risks.mitigation: Count a confirmed rapid-rehousing or NEXTenant unit as a valid next placement. Report unmet demand by program on the dashboard so the City sees where capacity, not coordination, is the limit.

risks.risk: Partners do not update the shared board, because HMIS bed-matching at Second Light is not live.
risks.mitigation: Navigators do the updating themselves at daily partner calls. Board entry is part of each partner agreement, and the partner-adoption marketing line funds staff training.

risks.risk: Landlords withdraw after a single bad tenancy, as Luis's demand for reduced risk suggests.
risks.mitigation: Give every landlord a single named contact with a written response window. Escalate tenant issues to case managers before eviction, building on the Prairie Wind practice [CHALLENGE_DATA: rehousing-options].

risks.risk: Youth disengage after enrollment, as with DCF IL's loss of [[q.84d8e]] participants after exit.
risks.mitigation: Pair each youth with a peer ambassador and a SOUL Family referral. Use text-based check-ins, and file KanCare address updates at every move.

brief_answers.answer: The dashboard shows four things: reachable beds against listed beds, free transition-program slots, the wait clock at each downstream program, and each person's position in the document chain. Today that means [[status001-reachable]] of [[status001-total]] emergency beds reachable, and [[free_beds_all]] free of [[beds_online_all]] beds online across facilities. It also means [[programs.free]] of [[programs.listed]] transition slots free, HumanKind waits of [[q.db126]] weeks, BRIDGES waits of [[q.536a6]] weeks, and Family Promise queues of [[q.970ad]] weeks. Navigators update it by hand until Second Light's HMIS bed-matching goes live.

Year 1 splits as follows: [[personnel_y1]] for navigators, [[ops_y1]] for document fees, bus passes and partner costs, and [[tech_y1]] for the shared board. It also covers [[outreach_y1]] for the brief's marketing reserve and [[indirect_y1]] in indirect costs at the de minimis rate, leaving [[contingency_y1]] held in contingency. Director oversight comes in kind from the coalition, so the personnel cap of [[cap.personnel_y1]] buys frontline navigators.

The page ranks options with a published Python table, not a model call. Beds are gated on being open, serving the household and age, meeting the site's own condition, and having a bed free. They are then weighted by fit for the group ([[prio.beds.built-for]]), free beds ([[prio.beds.free-beds]]), no referral needed ([[prio.beds.no-referral]]) and low-barrier entry ([[prio.beds.low-barrier]]). Transition programs weigh years before the age limit, weeks to start, participant retention and free slots ([[prio.programs.runway]] each). Doors weigh warm handoff ([[prio.doors.live-transfer]]), fit ([[prio.doors.built-for]]) and languages served ([[prio.doors.languages]]), because a door that cannot hand someone off or speak their language does not get them anywhere.

Youth handoffs fail at three points. At shelter exit, [[transition-programs.prog-006.transitionDropoutRate]] of CrossRoads exits have no confirmed next placement, because BRIDGES has [[q.ed5fc]] units and [[q.60225]] realistic admits. At the age cliff, DCF IL ends at [[q.cc62b]] and loses [[q.84d8e]] participants within [[q.4a2ab]] days of exit. At paperwork, the KanCare extension loses [[transition-programs.prog-003.transitionDropoutRate]] of enrollees to notices sent to old addresses, and a state ID takes at least [[state_id_days]] days from zero documents.

Python values what instability destroys: ER visits that kept coverage would avoid at [[ext.er_visit_cost]] each, expedited SNAP of [[q.e0e70]] left unclaimed, and ETV education funding left unused. The cost of inaction is [[coi_y1]] in Year 1, [[coi_y2]] in Year 2 and [[coi_y3]] in Year 3, totalling [[coi_3yr]] over [[plan.years]] years after deadweight of [[deadweight]]. Housing placement is material but not valued, because the data holds no local cost of a shelter night, so these figures understate the cost.

The pilot tracks four leading indicators weekly on the dashboard. The first is the share of CrossRoads exits with a confirmed next placement (target [[model:80%|target share of CrossRoads exits with a confirmed next placement]]). The second is the share of enrolled youth still covered by KanCare at pilot end (target [[model:85%|target share of enrolled former foster youth whose KanCare extension remains active at pilot end]]). The third is median days from zero documents to a state ID (target [[model:35|days, target median from no documents to state ID]]). The fourth is the share of referrals logged as warm handoffs (target [[model:75%|target share of referrals completed as logged warm handoffs]]). Volume is tracked against the Year-1 target of [[beneficiaries_y1]] people.

Renewal is earned if, at the end of the [[pilot_days]]-day pilot, the four KPI targets are met or trending toward them, and landlords and partners are still using the board. The base case projects Year 3 cost per person at [[cpb_y3]] and an SROI of [[sroi]]. The SROI is partial because housing is not valued. If the dashboard shows that downstream capacity, not coordination, is the limit, the renewal case says so plainly.

The pilot runs from June 1 to August 29, 2026, in three phases. June stands up the navigators, the partner case-sharing agreements and the bottleneck dashboard. July runs live handoffs for every CrossRoads exit, 211 Kansas after-hours loop and H.O.T. contact, with the document fast-lane and housing routing through NEXTenant, rapid rehousing, Housing First and VASH. August completes follow-ups and delivers the renewal recommendation against the KPI gate.

The [[reserve]] reserve is spent on trust and adoption across five lines. The two largest are landlord engagement through NEXTenant, with a single named contact and a risk-mitigation guide, and youth peer ambassadors with lived foster-care experience. The others are partner-staff training for warm handoffs, plain-language and Spanish materials on the N Market corridor, and participant listening sessions. Each line reports its own early signal: landlord pledges, youth self-referrals, staff trained, Spanish-language cases opened and process changes made from feedback.
